header.running_head: What Masaajid are Built for and what the Sahabah (RA) did therein

blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Praises the Gatherings in the Masaajid

Hadhrat Ibn Mu'aawiya Kindi reports that when he once went to see Hadhrat Umar (RA) in Shaam, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him about the condition of the people and said further, "Does it not happen that when a man enters the Masjid like an escaped camel and then sits with a group only if they belong to his tribe or if they are people whom he knows?" "Not at all," Hadhrat Ibn Mu'aawiya, replied, "In fact, there are several gatherings (in our Masjid) in which the people participate to learn and to rehearse good to each other." To this Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "You people will always remain in good stead as long as you remain like this." [^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Walks from the Masjid with the Sahabah (RA) to Address the Jews

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that they were sitting in the Masjid one day when Rasulullaah ﷺ came out of his room and said, "Let us go to the Jews." (When he reached them) Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Accept Islaam and you will live in peace. "But you have already conveyed this message to us," they replied. "But that is still what I want (that you people accept Islaam). So (I repeat) do accept Islaam and you will live in peace." Again the Jews responded by saying, "But you have already conveyed this message to us." "But that is still what I want," Rasulullaah ﷺ reiterated. When Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated himself for the third time (and they again refused to accept), he added, "You ought to know that the earth belongs to Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. I now wish to banish you from this land. Whoever wishes to sell any of his belongings may do so, otherwise you should bear in mind that the earth belongs to Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ." [^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ has Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) placed in the Masjid when the latter was Injured during the Battle of Khandaq

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) was injured during the Battle of Khandaq when a person by the name of Hibbaan bin Ariqah shot an arrow that struck Hadhrat Sa'd (RA)'s brachial artery. Rasulullaah ﷺ had a tent pitched for Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) in the Masjid so that he could be close by to visit him. When Nabi ﷺ returned from the Battle of Khandaq, he removed his armour and took a bath. It was then that Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, wiping dust off his head. "By Allaah!" Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) said, "You have already removed your armour whereas we (the angels) have not yet removed ours. March to them." "Where should we march?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked.
